scope: Eight complete measured arms; excludes warmup directories. Request classifications use request IDs and arrival timestamps only; output contents are not interpreted.
aggregation: Headline policy values are arithmetic means of the two per-run metrics (including per-run p95); no runs or requests are dropped. Matched deltas average each request across two runs per policy.

fixed2048.definition: feedback minus baseline; per-request time comparisons use two-run means matched by request_id

decode.definition: feedback minus baseline; per-request time comparisons use two-run means matched by request_id

fixed1024.definition: feedback minus baseline; per-request time comparisons use two-run means matched by request_id

interpretation: No request in any measured run violates the 100 ms observed-generation-gap SLO. The gap threshold does not drive the joint-goodput ordering.

Fixed2048 fails completion for 136/160 requests in each run; its 16 TTFT failures overlap completion failures. Feedback enables more early-wave completions while greatly extending later arrivals TTFT and tail completion.
The feedback gain over decode is a small discrete-threshold goodput increase, not a Pareto improvement: all requests finish, but total throughput falls and late-cohort waiting/completion increase.
Observed timings and selected budgets support a scheduling tradeoff explanation; two repeats do not establish statistical significance or model-output quality.
